source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 44 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, NVA1 through NVA3, with 420,000 square feet of technical space. That is enough to rank it fifteenth in Virginia by published megawatts, in a state this data counts at 2,563.4 MW across 29 facilities that publish a figure.

The pattern worth noting is the gap between what is mapped and what is measured. Virginia holds 376 mapped facilities but only 29 with a published capacity number. The facilities that publish are the ones large enough to be counted, and most of the physical buildout in the densest data center market in the country is invisible in capacity terms.

For AI specifically, the 44 MW figure is a power input, not an accelerator count. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 44 MW is roughly 1,100 racks. At a traditional 8 kW per rack it is about 5,500. The operator has not published a density, a tenant list, a power procurement method, or a delivery schedule, so the campus can be placed in the Virginia market but not sized in chips.

What the data does not cover: there is no address or postal code, no announced expansion, and no indication of who runs inside the buildings. The certifications, SOC 1 Type 2 through TIA-942, are permissions to host categories of work, not evidence that any particular tenant is present.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
